item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J01610","case1_error":"Omits the initial 50-yard width, treating 80 yards as the required increase.","case2_error":"Evaluates 18 + 6 + 8 + 7 as 49 instead of 39.","reason":"The first uses an incorrect width relation; the second numerically miscalculates a correctly written sum.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01611","case1_error":"Adds costs for 14 individual balloons and two packs, purchasing 34 balloons instead of exactly 14.","case2_error":"Gives unsupported final cost 4600 after correctly writing (60 × 8 × 14) + 2500, which yields 9220.","reason":"The first constructs an invalid purchase combination; the second supplies an incorrect final number after a correct formula without showing its calculation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01612","case1_error":"Evaluates 3000 × 8 / 6 as 2000 instead of 4000.","case2_error":"Gives unsupported final answer 80 after correct formulas imply four weeks.","reason":"The first explicitly miscalculates a written expression; the second provides a wrong final number without showing a numerical evaluation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01613","case1_error":"Counts Reece's ladder only once, omitting his 15 climbs from the total distance.","case2_error":"Assumes Lisa walks 24 hours daily despite the stated one hour daily.","reason":"The first omits a required repetition factor; the second introduces an unjustified duration factor by assuming continuous walking.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01614","case1_error":"Models five child tickets and five adult tickets instead of three child tickets and two adult tickets.","case2_error":"Gives unsupported final answer 6000 after correctly stating initial population plus ten times that population, which yields 5500.","reason":"The first writes an erroneous quantity relation; the second reports an unsupported wrong number after a correct relation.","judgment":"different"}]}
